props.eyebrow: Source code structure and data flow
props.title: Four entry points, one shared core
props.lead: The desktop app, local browser, CLI, and MCP share one TypeScript core and read and write the same local content library. This page explains the modules and how data flows between them.

content.text: Understand the data flow with one picture

People edit through the workbench, and agents edit through the CLI or MCP; the two paths converge at Core, which is the only place to read and write the content library. Click on a node to view its location in the source code.

nodes.label: user
nodes.detail: Read and edit pages in the desktop app or browser.

nodes.label: Agent
nodes.detail: Through the MCP tool operation page of the ShowAI plug-in; scripts and operation and maintenance scenarios directly call the CLI.

nodes.label: Desktop App
nodes.detail: The main process is at `src/desktop/main.ts `and the interface is at `src/studio `. The window configuration is saved in the system application data directory, and the page content is saved in the selected content library.

nodes.label: browser workbench
nodes.detail: `src/browser/server.ts `only listens to `127.0.0.1 `, uses HTTP to undertake workbench operations, and uses SSE to push file changes. The browser bridging layer converts original workbench calls into HTTP requests.

nodes.label: CLI
nodes.detail: `src/agent/cli.ts `,`scripts/cli.mjs `in the distribution package. Does not rely on resident services or open windows.

nodes.label: Shared workbench operation
nodes.detail: `src/workbench/actions.ts `: Electron calls the same implementation as the local browser service, so the behavior of the two workbenches is consistent.

nodes.label: Agent service
nodes.detail: `AgentService `shared by CLI and MCP in `src/agent/service.ts `: project parsing, page reading and writing, directory query, template, export, conflict recovery.

nodes.label: Core
nodes.detail: Storage (`store.ts `), semantic diff (`diff.ts `), component and template directory (`catalog.ts `), three-party merger (`catalog-merge.ts `), release verification (`publication.ts `).

nodes.label: Content Library
nodes.detail: The default is `.showai `in the user's home directory, which can be specified by App settings,`SHOWAI_HOME `or CLI's `--home `.

nodes.label: exporter
nodes.detail: `src/agent/exporter.ts `with reader `src/portable `. The component running code used by the page is collected only when exported.

nodes.label: project server
nodes.detail: Standalone shared HTTP service, supports Cloudflare Workers/D1/R2 and Linux Node.js/SQLite/Disk. The native workbench and CLI still use the local content library.

props.caption: Agent operation does not rely on desktop windows or resident services; the editor and standalone reader use the same page structure.

content.text: Before modifying a behavior, first find the layer it is in. Click on the module to view the responsibilities and source code path.

How to edit once without overwriting other people’s changes

Agent and user may modify the same page at the same time. Core uses content hashes and resource revisions to identify expired writes, and block ids to calculate differences so that the agent only needs to read the changed parts.

props.title: Agent and user edit a page at the same time

steps.label: read page
steps.detail: `page_read `or `pages read `. Reading retains a baseline for this session for later comparison.

steps.label: Return content and hash
steps.detail: Keep the hash, revision and stable block id, and bring them with you for subsequent writes.

steps.label: Modify and save in workbench
steps.detail: The editor saves drafts serially; the workbench refreshes affected content with file change notifications.

steps.label: Request difference by old hash
steps.detail: `page_diff `/`pages diff --since `. Core locally compares the baseline to the current content.

steps.label: List changes by block id
steps.detail: Add, delete, move and change fields. When the baseline cannot be found,`MISSING_BASELINE `is returned and the entire page needs to be reread.

steps.label: CONFLICT + current hash
steps.detail: Reject writing when the content has changed. The CLI ends with exit code 3. You can't just refresh the hash and overwrite it with the old document.

steps.label: Reread and merge
steps.detail: Reread the current page and compare the differences to incorporate your changes instead of overwriting the old document.

steps.label: Submit again with new hash
steps.detail: Saved successfully with current hash and revision; user's modifications are retained.

content.text: Controlled writes between the app and CLI use locks, hash checking, and temporary file replacement. Programs that bypass them and modify files directly should retain block IDs and use atomic replacement, otherwise no conflict guarantees will be obtained. For conflict resolution methods, see
